## Where does the split come from? {.psf-lesson}

We are learning to factorise non-monic quadratics by splitting the middle term. I can choose the signed pair, group the terms and expand to check.

1. Expand $(2x+3)(x+2)$ using FOIL.
2. Circle the terms that combine to give $7x$.

::: {.fragment}

$(2x+3)(x+2)=2x^2+4x+3x+6=2x^2+7x+6$

:::

::: {.fragment}

Read backwards. The cross products give the split $7x=4x+3x$. The coefficients multiply to $2(6)=12$ and add to $7$.

:::

::: {.fragment}

For $ax^2+bx+c$:

1. Record $P=ac$ and $S=b$.
2. Choose the signed factors of P whose sum is S.
3. Use the pair to split $bx$, then group matching brackets.

:::
